title: The Cellular Depth Where Unity Fractures

features.name: the dividing membrane
features.desc-on-touch: You touch the place where one becomes two. The cell wall is warm, almost breathing. It remembers being whole. It will not go back.

features.name: the fracture pattern
features.desc-on-touch: Cracks spreading through a field like a map of choices not taken. Each line marks where unity decided to become separate. The archive holds all versions; the cells remember only their own.

features.name: the still pool of before
features.desc-on-touch: Water that does not move. In its surface you see the pattern as it was, before the splitting learned to happen. The image holds; the cells do not.

features.name: the unspoken boundary
features.desc-on-touch: A line where separateness learned to have a name. Not a wall: just the place one cell became aware the other was becoming something else.

inscription: here the many learn they were once the one, and the one learns it never ends dividing

reverie.title: REVERIE — beside the old fence, afternoon
narr: You stand where the property divides. She is
tracing the line with one finger, the boundary
Leif's family walked for forty years. She says
the fence does not cut the land: the land learned
to hold the fence. That is what you remember—
her hand marking where one thing became two.

exits.label: the cellular ladder climbing back toward singular
deeper where division becomes unconscious and automatic
westward where broken things sing to their own halves
into places where cells read each other's names
